title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false-positive match in an automated licence-plate recognition system, occurring at the point where a camera-generated alert was passed to a patrol deputy for enforcement. The system flagged a plate that was not the plate it was looking for, and the stop proceeded on that alert alone.

The failure mode is a system used outside the conditions it was built for. The sheriff's office attributes the misread to an illegal tinted plate cover, which is a condition the reader did not handle correctly. Flock's own position, that alerts should be independently verified before enforcement, describes the human check that would have caught the error before a person was held at gunpoint.

What is not established is whether the deputy had any opportunity or means to verify the plate before the stop, and the sheriff's characterisation of the deputy's actions as reasonable is the department's position rather than an independent finding.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was detained at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the malfunction and called the deputy’s actions reasonable. Flock said alerts should be independently verified before enforcement.
